contract.authorization: The app that owns the slot, while the slot still runs on its own dashboard:<slot> session. Every other case, a missing slot included, is the same 404.
contract.completedToolEvents: The stop appends one system row and edits only that row. Rows already in the slot window, completed tool_call and tool_result rows included, are left byte-identical and queued messages stay queued on a cooperative stop.

confirmationEvent.ambiguity: When the turn had already ended the card still settles as stopped; only the HTTP reply (info: no active turn) tells the two apart. Require both the reply without info and the settled card.

confirmed.meaning: no ack in budget; session reset

confirmationEvent.identity: meta.id (stop-<hex>): the same id on the opening and the settling frame, and on the one history row. The HTTP reply does not return it.
confirmationEvent.notAConfirmation: chat_done has slot, turn, turn_gen, continuing and needs_input only: it ends every turn alike and never says a turn was stopped.

neverSend: a second POST while the first is unanswered

successResponse.turnWasStopped: ok is true and there is no info key. The reply is sent only after the cancel settled, by acknowledgement or by Crew resetting the session.

decision.flagFlipsOnlyAfter: the owner's live step reproduces the request, the settled stop_event frame and the preserved tool rows
decision.summary: The stop request, its owner-app scope, its replies and the stop_event confirmation frame are proven against Crew's packaged handlers, but not against a live session. The design's fail-closed fallback applies: Cancel stays disabled with contract_unavailable until the owner runs the live step.

inferred: The token middleware publishes the app claim the checkpoint reads (the probe sets it directly). S6 verified live that the same app token and grants reach /api/chat/slots/{slot}/project, a sibling route under the same owner-app policy.
An app-token socket on /api/ws receives the stop card frame with its meta: chat_message is a slot-scoped event (dashboard/ws_event_scope.py), and S6 received chat_* frames live.

After an acknowledged cancel the turn runner appends a done row, pushes a slots frame with running false and sends chat_done (dashboard/chat_turn/queue_cycle.py); partial reply text and completed tool rows stay, as the product documentation for Stop states.
An unacknowledged cancel makes Crew reset the session and start a fresh agent process (session_lifecycle_parts/turn_stop.py); the transcript rows stay, the agent's context does not.
A pending tool approval on the stopped turn is rejected by the stop (turn_stop.py _reject_pending_approvals), so an approval card never outlives it.

verified: Crew's packaged chat route table registers POST /api/chat/slots/{slot}/stop on api_chat_slot_stop, with POST only, next to a separate /interrupt route.
Crew's packaged scope matcher admits the stop path for an installed app whose manifest grants /api/chat and /api/chat/*, and refuses an installed app without them.

Through the packaged router and slot-ownership checkpoint, an app caller stops only a slot it owns that still runs on its own session; another app's slot, the owner's own chat, an owned slot linked to a foreign session and a missing slot all answer the same 404 slot_not_found, and a refused stop changes nothing.
The packaged stop handler takes no body, asks the session manager for a cooperative cancel of dashboard:<slot> with the queue preserved, and answers {ok: true} after that call returns.

The stop appends one system row whose meta is {kind: stop_event, id, state, outcome, ts_start}; it is broadcast as a chat_message frame in state stopping and again, same id, in state stopped with outcome soft once the cancel is acknowledged.
Rows already in the slot window (user, tool_call, tool_result) are byte-identical after the stop, cooperative or forced.
A stop on an idle slot answers info: not running with no card; a turn that already ended answers info: no active turn; a compacting session answers info: compacting and is not stopped.
A second POST while the first is still pending makes the handler ask for a forced stop and empties the slot's queue; ?force=true on a first POST stays cooperative.
The packaged chat_done payload has no stop or cancel marker.
The default soft-stop budget in Crew's packaged config is 10 seconds.

guidance.afterwards: Never reuse a stopped slot for the retry; the design already requires a fresh slot and a higher Run_Sequence.
guidance.confirm: Treat cancellation as confirmed only when the reply is {ok: true} with no info key and a stop_event frame for the bound slot reached stopped, force_stopped or stop_failed_reset. Then submit run_blocked with reason cancelled.
guidance.manifest: No change. The existing /api/chat and /api/chat/* grants cover the route.
guidance.ownerStop: The owner's own Stop on the same slot produces the same card. A settled stop_event on a bound slot with an active run is a cancellation whoever asked.
guidance.request: Send one bodyless POST per cancellation with a client timeout of at least 30 seconds (the owner can raise Crew's soft-stop budget from 10 up to 60 seconds; a reply later than 30 seconds is cancel_unconfirmed by design). Never retry it and never send force=true: a repeat while the first is pending is a forced stop that resets the session and discards its queue.
guidance.unconfirmed: A reply carrying info, a 404, a transport error, a declined (compacting) card or no settled card within 30 seconds is cancel_unconfirmed: keep the claim.
